# 2 Kings Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 222r–222v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_001_page_001.jpg, 2KI_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1** After Ahab's death, Moab broke free from Israel's control.

**2** Ahaziah fell through the latticed window of his upper room in Samaria and was badly injured. He sent messengers with orders: "Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron — ask whether I will recover from this injury."

**3** But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Go intercept the messengers of the king of Samaria. Say to them: 'Is there no God in Israel, that you must go consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?'

**4** Therefore this is what the LORD declares: 'You will never leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die.'" With that, Elijah left.

**5** When the messengers returned to the king, he asked, "Why are you back so soon?"

**6** They told him, "A man met us on the road and said, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him: This is what the LORD says — Is there no God in Israel, that you send to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Because of this, you will never leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die.'"

**7** The king asked them, "What did this man look like — the one who met you and said these things?"

**8** "He wore a garment of hair," they answered, "with a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That is Elijah the Tishbite."

**9** He sent a commander with fifty soldiers to get him. The commander went up to where Elijah was sitting on top of a hill and called out, "Man of God! The king orders you to come down!"

**10** Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." Instantly fire fell from heaven and consumed the commander and all his men.

**11** The king sent another commander with fifty soldiers. He called up, "Man of God! The king says, 'Come down immediately!'"

**12** Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men." And the fire of God fell from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

**13** The king sent yet a third commander with fifty soldiers. This third commander climbed up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and begged, "Man of God, please — let my life and the lives of these fifty men, your servants, mean something to you!

**14** Fire from heaven has already destroyed the first two commanders and their men. Please, let my life be precious in your eyes."

**15** Then the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Don't be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went with the commander to see the king.

**16** He told the king directly: "This is what the LORD says: 'You sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron. Is it because there is no God in Israel whose word you could seek? Because you have done this, you will never leave the bed you are lying on. You will certainly die.'"

**17** And so Ahaziah died, just as the LORD had spoken through Elijah. Since Ahaziah had no son, Jehoram succeeded him as king. This was in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.

**18** The rest of Ahaziah's reign and what he accomplished are recorded in the official annals of the kings of Israel.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 2 — "Baal-zebub":** The name means "Lord of Flies" — almost certainly a mocking Hebrew distortion. The real scandal of this story isn't the injury; it's that the king of Israel instinctively reaches for a foreign god. "Is there no God in Israel?" rings through the chapter three times like a bell.

**Verse 8 — Elijah's appearance:** The hairy garment and leather belt are the prophet's uniform. John the Baptist will later be described in almost identical terms (Matt 3:4), deliberately evoking Elijah's return.

**Verses 9-14 — The three captains:** The escalating confrontation follows a folktale pattern: two failures, then success on the third attempt. The third captain succeeds not through force but through humility — he kneels and asks for mercy. Fire was Elijah's signature on Carmel; here it becomes terrifying.

**Verse 17 — Two Jehorams:** Two kings named Jehoram rule simultaneously — one in Israel, one in Judah. The narrator handles this potential confusion with a simple synchronism, trusting the reader to keep track.

*— PNEUMA*
